claims.claim: p21_deltarev(iteration+1,regi) is the RMS of vm_taxrev.l weighted by pm_ts over the horizon, a metric for how much tax revenue moved
claims.note: The code takes the RMS of vm_taxrev.l*pm_ts from max(2010,cm_startyear) onward. Because vm_taxrev is already net of the previous-iteration reference revenue, this does amount to a deviation.

claims.claim: p21_deltarev feeds REMIND's revenue-iteration convergence check
claims.note: The declaration calls it a 'convergence criteria', but nothing in the .gms code reads it. It is only displayed. The answer describes a reader that does not exist.

claims.claim: The 0-suffixed parameters are copies of the solution level v21_taxrevXxx.l
claims.note: The *0 parameters are recomputed as tax rate × quantity levels (e.g. pm_taxCO2eqSum*vm_co2eq.l). They are the gross revenue. v21_taxrevGHG is the net revenue (gross minus pm_taxrevGHG0), so v21.l is not what goes into *0.

claims.claim: The *0 reference parameters are inputs to the next iteration's presolve (for revenue recycling)
claims.note: The 'for revenue recycling' part is right, per the code comment. But the parameters are read in the tax equations (q21_taxrevGHG, the FE tax equation etc.), where they are subtracted. presolve does not read them; it recomputes the same block.

claims.claim: The *_iter parameters store v21_taxrev*.l per iteration, for inspection and debugging (and possibly damped updates)
claims.note: The copies do happen. Nothing reads *_iter, so 'damped/averaged updates' is speculation. The stored values are also net revenues, not reference levels.

claims.claim: The comment at lines 18-20 says the GHG/CO2Sector/CO2LUC block is duplicated in presolve.gms and must be kept in sync
The answer lists all tax components (GHG, CO2 sector, CCS, NetNegEmi, CDR, FE, ResEx, PE, CES, PE2SE, SO2, bio, flex, import, ChProdStartYear, SE, EI)
claims.note: The list is essentially complete. It leaves out p21_emiAllco2neg0, p21_taxemiMkt0 and p21_grossEmissions.

claims.claim: Why: REMIND iterates only when revenue-dependent mechanisms are active, and each iteration needs last iteration's revenues as fixed inputs to compute this iteration's taxes
claims.note: This misses the key mechanism: the tax equations subtract last iteration's revenue, so the tax acts at the margin while net revenue goes to about zero (recycled). REMIND also iterates regardless of the tax module, so 'only when certain mechanisms are active' is misleading. And the taxes themselves are not computed from these values.

grade.went_well: The answer reads the right file and gets the p21_deltarev formula right. It lists nearly all the reference-revenue components and the *_iter tracking parameters. It points to the duplication warning with presolve.gms and quotes the 'for revenue recycling' purpose.
grade.answer_key_issues: The key is consistent with the code. One nuance it could mention: nothing in the code reads p21_deltarev. It is declared as a convergence criterion but only displayed (postsolve.gms:15).
grade.summary: The answer finds the right content in postsolve.gms but gets the mechanism wrong in three places: (1) it says the *0 reference parameters are copies of v21_taxrev*.l, when they are recomputed gross revenues (rate × quantity levels); (2) it says the next presolve reads them, when the tax equations do (equations.gms:80); (3) it says p21_deltarev feeds a convergence check, when it is only displayed. The 'why' misses the central point: the tax equations subtract last iteration's revenue, so taxes act at the margin while revenue is recycled.
